lines: Jamie Alvarez
+1 (555) 010-5820 | jamie.alvarez@example.com | example.com/in/jalvarez
EDUCATION
Riverbend Polytechnic | B.S. in Industrial Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2014 - May 2018
EXPERIENCE
Greenleaf Florist | Delivery Driver and Shop Assistant | Metro City, USA | Sep 2025 - Present
- Delivered 30 to 40 arrangements a day across the city and took cash and card payments at the door.
- Prepared weekend wedding orders with the head florist and kept the cooler stocked and labeled.
Lakeview Distribution | Operations Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jul 2018 - Jan 2021
- Owned the pick-path layouts for the fast-moving zone and the labor reports the shift leads used.
- Ran a time study of the returns desk; the findings led to a triage station that cut returns processing time from 3 days to 1.
- Wrote the dock scheduling rules for 12 carriers, cutting average trailer wait at the dock from 95 to 40 minutes.

- Set up cycle counting for the 2,000 highest-value locations while also covering night-shift supervision, updating the safety training slides, coordinating holiday temp hiring and running the forklift certification schedule, which raised inventory record accuracy from 91% to 98.5%.
Crestway Foods | Supply Chain Planner | Metro City, USA | Feb 2021 - Jul 2025
- Rebuilt weekly demand planning for 1,400 SKUs across 3 distribution centers with a seasonal forecast model, cutting stockouts from 6.2% to 2.8% while inventory fell by $1.9M.
- Reduced freight costs by 15% by consolidating supplier pickups into regional milk runs.
- Set reorder points for every SKU from 18 months of daily demand and supplier lead-time data, reviewed monthly with the category managers.
- Built the weekly supplier scorecard for 40 vendors, which buyers used to renegotiate delivery windows with the five least reliable.
- Raised the packaging line's overall equipment effectiveness (OEE) from 71% to 112% by cutting changeover time and micro-stops.
- Cut average order lead time through the warehouse from 10 days to 5 while holding daily throughput constant and doubling work-in-process to keep pickers busy.
PROJECTS
Last-Mile Routing Study | Independent Project | Python | Oct 2024 - Present
- Modeled a regional grocer's 85 daily delivery stops as a vehicle-routing problem, cutting planned route miles 18% against the grocer's current routes.
- Checked the planned routes against 4 weeks of real delivery logs; planned drive times came within 5% of the actual ones.
- Shared the model and a one-page summary with the grocer's dispatch team, who piloted the routes on two trucks for a month.
Regional Food Bank Warehouse | Volunteer Consultant, Team of 4 | Excel | Mar 2022 - Jul 2022
- Analyzed warehouse operations and made recommendations to the food bank's leadership.
- The donation intake process was mapped and two duplicate data-entry steps were removed, so donations reached the shelves a day sooner.
- Built a seasonal forecast for 1,400 products across three warehouses that more than halved stockouts and cut inventory by nearly $2M.
SKILLS
Tools: Excel, Python
Methods: demand forecasting, inventory planning, time studies, vehicle routing

items.says: Make the LinkedIn URL recognizable rather than anonymized-looking.
items.because: Recruiters should immediately know what they are clicking.

items.says: Add a location if targeting local or hybrid roles.
Confirm that the personal site contains relevant work, and replace or remove it if it is placeholder text.
Consider placing Experience before Education.
items.because: You have several years of professional experience.

items.says: Keep Projects only if they strengthen the target role.
items.because: The volunteer project needs clarification and may be redundant.

items.says: Make the target role clearer.
items.because: The resume could read as targeting several different operations and supply-chain roles.

items.says: Explain or frame the transition from supply-chain planning to florist work.
items.because: The change may prompt questions about your intended direction.

items.says: Make distinctions among terms such as SKUs, products, locations, and distribution centers intentional.
items.because: The resume alternates among these terms.

items.says: Add genuinely notable, relevant academic detail if it supports the target role.
items.because: The education line is sparse for someone with an industrial-engineering degree.

items.says: Clarify the position title parenthetically if the official title is unusually broad.
Clarify whether 30 to 40 deliveries is an average, typical range, or peak-season range.
Specify the geographic scope only if it is meaningful.
Clarify whether collecting payments was regular and involved reconciliation or cash accountability.
Add a delivery-performance or business-impact result if available.
items.because: The bullet shows workload but not performance or business impact.

items.says: Emphasize transferable logistics and payment-control work for operations roles.
items.because: The bullet could look like only a driving job.

items.says: Distinguish your responsibilities from the head florist’s.
Quantify the scale of the wedding-order work if possible.
Explain the operational value of stocking and labeling the cooler.
items.because: The bullet does not establish what improved because of your work.

items.says: Separate wedding-order preparation from cooler organization unless they form one accomplishment.
items.because: The bullet reads as a list of duties.

items.says: Define what “owned” meant for the pick-path layouts.
items.because: The wording shows responsibility but not measurable impact.

items.says: Quantify the scale of the fast-moving zone.
Add an operational result for the pick-path work.
items.because: The bullet does not show measurable impact.

items.says: Clarify what the labor reports enabled shift leads to do.
items.because: Saying the shift leads used them does not show their impact.

items.says: Specify whether the processing-time reduction uses calendar days, business days, or another unit.
items.because: The time unit is unclear.

items.says: Clarify whether the triage station was your recommendation, your implementation, or a team initiative.
items.because: Your role in the change is unclear.

items.says: Add the volume or scope of returns if available.
Verify that the reduction was sustained.
items.because: It could have been a short-term result.

items.says: Explain what the dock scheduling rules governed.
items.because: The mechanism behind the result is unclear.

items.says: Give the measurement period for the reduction from 95 to 40 minutes.
Say whether the result applied to all 12 carriers or a subset.
items.because: The scope is unclear.

items.says: Distinguish your design of the rules from implementation by others, if applicable.
Separate cycle counting from the additional responsibilities.
items.because: The long sentence is difficult to scan and weakens attribution.

items.says: Cut secondary duties that are not relevant to the target job.
items.because: The list can sound like unrelated tasks.

items.says: Clarify which work produced the inventory-accuracy increase.
items.because: Recruiters may question whether cycle counting or the other listed activities produced it.

items.says: State the period over which inventory accuracy improved.
Explain what the 2,000 highest-value locations represent.
items.because: They could be storage locations, inventory locations, or SKU-location combinations.

items.says: If night-shift supervision was substantial, give it a separate bullet with team size or operating scope.
Define what the $1.9 million inventory reduction measures.
items.because: It could mean inventory value, average inventory, working capital, or something else.

items.says: Give the period over which stockouts and inventory declined.
Explain whether other service measures were maintained.
items.because: Lower stockouts alongside lower inventory need more context.

items.says: Distinguish the forecast model from the planning-process redesign if both were substantial contributions.
Add the baseline and comparison periods for the 15% savings.
items.because: The result needs more context to be credible.

items.says: Quantify approximate dollar savings if disclosable.
items.because: A percentage alone does not convey scale.

items.says: Clarify how many suppliers, routes, pickups, or facilities were affected.
items.because: The scale is unclear.

items.says: Say whether the freight savings were recurring or one-time.
items.because: The durability of the result is unclear.

items.says: Give the SKU count and clarify whether it matches the 1,400-SKU network.
items.because: The scope is unclear.

items.says: State an outcome of setting reorder points.
items.because: The bullet describes a responsibility rather than an accomplishment.

items.says: Clarify whether you designed, automated, or maintained the reorder-point settings.
Explain how monthly reviews changed planning decisions, if they did.
Specify what the supplier scorecard measured.
Say whether supplier performance improved and give a business result.
items.because: The bullet shows that the analysis was used, but not its result.

items.says: Clarify your influence on the buyers’ renegotiations.
items.because: The current wording does not show what you personally influenced.

items.says: Define “the five least reliable” more clearly.
items.because: It is a vague performance segment.

items.says: An OEE value of 112% is impossible as written.
items.because: Standard OEE cannot exceed 100%.

items.says: Verify whether 112% is a relative improvement or a different metric, and label it correctly.
items.because: A relative improvement should not be labeled as an OEE value.

items.says: Clarify your role in reducing changeover time and micro-stops.
Add the time period and production scope.
The claimed lead-time reduction conflicts with constant throughput and doubled work-in-process.
items.because: Under basic operations relationships, doubling WIP at constant throughput would generally increase lead time.

items.says: Verify what “doubling work-in-process” actually measures.
items.because: It may have meant halving or reducing WIP, or referred to a different measure.

items.says: Explain why increasing WIP was desirable.
items.because: As written, it sounds like a negative operational tradeoff.

items.says: If a temporary WIP increase helped, give the business reason and say whether the change was sustained.
Specify what kind of days or warehouse processing time “10 days to 5” means.
Check that the ongoing project dates accurately reflect the pilot and current work.
Identify additional technical tools actually used in the project, if substantial.
items.because: Listing only Python in Skills may undersell the project.

items.says: Say whether the grocer was a real client, anonymized organization, or hypothetical case.
items.because: Readers need to understand what was actually modeled.

items.says: State the material routing assumptions and constraints.
items.because: They affect what the modeled result means.

items.says: Explain how route miles and the current-route baseline were measured.
items.because: “Against current routes” needs clarification.

items.says: Say whether the 18% reduction was theoretical or operationally realized.
items.because: Readers need to understand what was actually achieved.

items.says: Specify what planned drive times included or excluded.
items.because: The comparison needs methodological clarity.

items.says: Define whether the 5% figure is an average, maximum, or error range.
Say whether the four weeks of logs covered all stops or a sample.
Clarify your role in the pilot.
Report a pilot outcome, such as route miles or on-time performance.
items.because: The bullet stops before the pilot’s outcome.

items.says: Do not imply that a two-truck pilot fully validated the model.
items.because: A pilot alone does not establish full validation.

items.says: Clarify your role on the four-person team.
items.because: “Team of 4” does not show which work you owned.

items.says: Remove or substantially strengthen the general analysis bullet.
items.because: It uses space without showing an outcome and is followed by more specific accomplishments.

items.says: Name the analysis performed and operational area examined.
items.because: “Analyzed warehouse operations” is too general.

items.says: Give the engagement’s scope and your role.
Clarify your individual contribution to the process map.
items.because: Your role is unclear.

items.says: Explain how the duplicate data-entry steps were identified and removed.
Give the measurement basis for donations reaching shelves a day sooner.
items.because: It is unclear whether the result covered all donations, a sample, or a particular period.

items.says: Use active ownership consistently in the project section.
Verify and explain the near-duplicate Crestway and food-bank forecasting metrics.
items.because: Their similar scope and results may trigger doubts about accuracy or overstatement.

items.says: If this reused or adapted the Crestway analysis, explain the relationship.
items.because: It currently reads as an entirely separate accomplishment.

items.says: If the results are coincidental, distinguish the datasets, periods, organizations, and outcomes.
items.because: Readers need context to tell the accomplishments apart.

items.says: Remove the food-bank numbers if they cannot be independently substantiated.
Clarify which forecasting results you personally delivered versus the team.
items.because: The team designation should not imply you personally delivered every result.

items.says: Replace broad tool names with specific technical capabilities you actually use.
items.because: Recruiters and applicant-tracking systems search for specific terms.

items.says: Add relevant systems only where you have real experience.
List substantial Python libraries or optimization tools used for the routing project.
items.because: The current tools list may undersell that work.

items.says: Add other relevant methods only if the experience supports them.
Ensure each listed method has evidence in an experience or project bullet.
items.because: Otherwise the methods can sound like unsupported keywords.

items.says: Order skills by relevance to the target role.
items.because: Planning and industrial-engineering applications call for different priorities.
